session_start.title: Start a plug session
session_start.description:
Move a smart plug onto the device you want to teach. While the session is active, a candidate target's plug reading is subtracted from the remainder; a confirmed device's own sensors and validation keep running and the plug is recorded for the session window.

The session stays open until you end it, or automatically on the end date you set. Earlier sessions are never changed when the plug moves on.

data_description.plug: Any power sensor that is not already an Energy dashboard source or metered device.
data_description.target: A candidate from the last learning run, or a confirmed device.
data_description.end_date: The session ends automatically at this date and time. Leave empty to end it by hand.

session_end.title: End a plug session
session_end.description: Ending the session stops subtracting its plug from the remainder and closes the recorded window. Its earlier data stays in the buffer.

review.title: Review device candidates
review.description: Candidates from the last learning run, ranked by the share of unexplained energy they explain. The figures are local consistency checks on training and validation days; measured accuracy against real plug readings comes in a later version. Pick a candidate, then close the dialog when you are done.{captures_notice}

menu_options.merge: Merge another confirmed device into it

rollback.title: Restore parameter version
rollback.description:
{candidate}

The device keeps its sensors, entity IDs and energy total; only the detection parameters change.

confirm.title: Confirm device
confirm.description:
{candidate}{warning}

Confirming creates a device with power and energy sensors that PowerGuesser estimates locally.

merge.title: Merge candidates
merge.description: The selected candidates are combined into {candidate}. They will no longer be listed, and later learning runs map them to this candidate. The shares and scores shown update at the next learning run. A merged confirmed device is retired: its energy sensor keeps its last value and its power sensor becomes unavailable. Delete it under Settings when you no longer need its history. Merging a candidate into a confirmed device retrains the device locally in the background; the new parameters are kept only if they are at least as good, and the device keeps its sensors and history either way.

data.sources: Candidates to merge into this one

learning.title: Learning options
learning.description: Configure token caps, cost limits, schedule, and data sharing for PowerGuesser device learning.

data_description.share_entity_names: When enabled, names and areas of metered plugs are sent to the LLM to improve candidate labels.
data_description.max_tokens_per_call: Upper limit for one LLM reply. Reasoning models spend hidden reasoning tokens inside this limit; if learning fails with output_truncated, raise it (the default 32000 suits reasoning models).
data_description.truncation_guard: Abort and notify if the endpoint reports implausibly few prompt tokens for the payload size.
data_description.validate_after_learning: Runs the local holdout validation after every successful learning run. It sends nothing to the LLM.

phases.title: Per-phase power (optional)
phases.description:
If your energy meter provides active power for individual grid phases (L1, L2, L3), you may map one to three phases here to record and profile per-phase data. Leave a field empty to clear that phase mapping. Gross and remainder power keep using total power either way.

Power sensors on your grid meter's device: {grid_device_sensors}

llm_endpoint.title: LLM endpoint
llm_endpoint.description:
PowerGuesser uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint only to learn device patterns; day-to-day detection stays local. Enter the base URL (ending in /v1), the API key if the endpoint needs one, and the model id.

Saving runs a short capability test that sends only a fixed test prompt, no household data, and stores which structured-output method the endpoint supports. Leave the base URL empty to disable learning.

data_description.llm_api_key: Leave empty to keep the stored key. The stored key is kept only while the scheme, host and port stay the same; otherwise enter it again. Most local servers need no key.
data_description.llm_clear_key: Turn on to save the endpoint without an API key. A key typed above is still used.

phase_check.title: Check phase mapping
phase_check.description:
The mapped phases add up to {phase_sum} W while grid power reads {grid} W (result: {result}).

The comparison uses each sensor's latest reading, which can be up to a minute old on slow meters, so a mismatch right after a load change is expected. Re-opening the dialog later gives a fresh comparison. A sum close to the negative of grid power means the phase sensors use the opposite sign and Invert phase sign should be on. Mapping only some phases of a three-phase supply makes a mismatch expected. The mapping can be saved either way.

progress.probe: Testing the endpoint. Slow local models can take a minute or more.

abort.no_candidates: There are no candidates to review yet. Run learning first.

no_energy_prefs.title: No gross power sources in Energy dashboard
no_energy_prefs.description: No grid, solar, battery, or home power source is configured in your Energy dashboard. Gross and remainder power will stay unavailable until a power source is configured in the Energy dashboard.

missing_stat_rate.title: Missing power rate for {source}
missing_stat_rate.description: The Energy dashboard source {source} lacks a power sensor. Gross and remainder power will stay unavailable until a power sensor is configured for this source in the Energy dashboard.

unsupported_power_config.title: Unsupported power configuration for {source}
unsupported_power_config.description: The Energy dashboard source {source} has an unsupported power configuration. Gross and remainder power will stay unavailable until the configuration is corrected in the Energy dashboard.

source_not_found.title: Power source entity not found for {source}
source_not_found.description: The power entity for {source} is not registered or present in Home Assistant. Gross and remainder power will stay unavailable until this source is available.

invalid_unit.title: Invalid power unit for {source}
invalid_unit.description: The power entity for {source} does not report a valid power unit (e.g. W or kW). Gross and remainder power will stay unavailable until a valid power sensor is configured in the Energy dashboard.

self_reference.title: Self-referencing entity {entity}
self_reference.description: PowerGuesser entity {entity} cannot be used as an input source or metered device in the Energy dashboard. Remove it from your Energy dashboard configuration.

metered_no_power.title: No power sensor for {device}
metered_no_power.description: The metered device {device} is not subtracted from gross power until a power rate sensor is configured in the Energy dashboard, or the device has exactly one power sensor in W or kW.

implausible_negative_gross.title: Implausible negative gross power
implausible_negative_gross.description: Gross home power has been consistently negative. Likely causes include: an inverted grid power sensor (net export instead of net import), battery charge and discharge directions swapped, or solar measured on the DC side instead of AC consumption. Check your power sensor configuration in the Energy dashboard. This issue clears automatically after about 12 hours of plausible readings, or immediately when the Energy dashboard is edited.

implausible_metered_above_gross.title: Metered power exceeds gross power
implausible_metered_above_gross.description: The sum of metered consumer devices consistently exceeds gross household power. Likely causes include: metered devices counted twice in the device hierarchy, a smart plug power sensor reporting in the wrong unit, or an inverted battery/solar source sign. Check your device and power sensor configuration in the Energy dashboard. This issue clears automatically after about 12 hours of plausible readings, or immediately when the Energy dashboard is edited.

buffer_reset.title: PowerGuesser started a new data buffer
buffer_reset.description: The existing buffer file could not be read (for example after a power cut or SD-card fault). It was kept as {backup} in the powerguesser folder of the configuration directory. Collected history starts again from now, and the notice disappears after the next restart.

capture_orphans.title: Captured runs have no target
capture_orphans.description: {count} captured run(s): target no longer exists: reassign or delete them with the PowerGuesser capture actions (capture_reassign, capture_delete).

llm_auth.title: PowerGuesser cannot sign in to the LLM endpoint

confirm.title: Update the LLM API key
confirm.description:
The endpoint at {host} rejected the API key, so learning stopped. Gross power, remainder and the history buffer keep working.

Submit to open the PowerGuesser options, then choose LLM endpoint and enter a valid key.

learning_consent.title: Allow PowerGuesser to send power summaries to {endpoint}?

confirm.title: Confirm data sharing for learning
confirm.description:
Learning sends summaries of your household power data to {endpoint} ({location}, {transport}) for the model {model}:
- statistics per group of similar power steps (step size, duration, hour-of-day and weekday counts, energy share)
- reference sessions of devices that already have their own power meter
- in refinement rounds, how well each proposed device explained the training period

No raw readings, no timestamps, no entity ids. Device names: {names}.

Learning runs may include a masked validation pass: the same kind of summaries with the devices that have their own power meter mixed back in and no reference sessions, used only to measure accuracy on this installation.

The first request is {bytes} bytes; a deliberately conservative estimate puts it at up to about {tokens} tokens (providers usually count fewer). The provider may keep requests according to its own terms.

To see the exact request first, run the action "PowerGuesser: Preview learning payload" under Developer tools > Actions.

Submit to allow learning with this endpoint. Changing the endpoint scheme, host or port, or the device-names setting, asks again.

abort.endpoint_changed: The endpoint or the device-names setting changed. A new notice for the current settings has been created.

learning_capped.title: PowerGuesser learning stopped at a limit
learning_capped.description: Learning stopped before sending another request because the {cap} limit ({limit}) would have been exceeded. Raise the limit under the PowerGuesser options, Learning, or wait for the monthly reset. This notice clears after the next completed run or when a new month starts.

detection_interval_too_slow.title: Sampling too slow for device detection
detection_interval_too_slow.description: Your power readings arrive about every {interval} s. Device detection needs a reading at least every {max_interval} s, so it is paused for {devices}: their power sensors are unavailable and their energy sensors keep their totals. If your meter integration lets you, shorten its update interval. This message disappears by itself once readings arrive often enough.

device_record_missing.title: PowerGuesser device {name} has no saved data
device_record_missing.description: The device {name} exists but its learned parameters were not found (for example after restoring an older backup). Its sensors stay unavailable. Delete the device under Settings, PowerGuesser, then confirm the candidate again in Review.

retired_device_in_energy.title: Merged device {name} is still in the Energy dashboard
retired_device_in_energy.description: {name} was merged into {target} and no longer estimates energy. Its sensor {entity} keeps its last value. Replace it with the energy sensor of {target} in the Energy dashboard when you are ready; its past consumption stays in your history.

reconfigure.title: Rename device
reconfigure.description: The sensors keep their entity IDs and history.

abort.use_review: Devices are created by confirming a candidate under Configure, Review candidates.

error.name_invalid: Enter a name of 1 to 64 characters without control characters.

learn.name: Learn devices
learn.description: Starts a learning run in the background. Needs an LLM endpoint, a confirmed data-sharing notice and at least 7 days of usable history.

preview_learning_payload.name: Preview learning payload
preview_learning_payload.description: Returns the exact request body that the next learning run would send to the LLM endpoint, without sending anything. The API key and headers are never included.

run_validation.name: Run validation
run_validation.description: Measures each plug-metered device's estimate against its own plug readings over the most recent holdout window and returns the report. Runs locally, sends nothing to the LLM.

synthetic_overlap.name: Add synthetic overlap
synthetic_overlap.description: Adds a clearly labelled synthetic overlap block by time-shifting one plug onto another. Real figures are not changed.

capture_window.name: Capture a window
capture_window.description: Snaps a past start/end window to the real rise and fall edges of a device run, stores the capture and returns it. Captures stay local and appear in Review as a preview candidate.

start.name: Start
start.description: The local start time of the run (interpreted in the Home Assistant time zone).

end.name: End
end.description: The local end time of the run.

label.name: Label
label.description: A short label for this capture.

target_type.name: Target type
target_type.description: What the capture teaches: a new device, an existing Review candidate, or a confirmed device.

target.name: Target
target.description: A new device's name; a candidate's name or signature id; a confirmed device's name or uuid when no device is picked.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Pick a confirmed PowerGuesser device (a shortcut for a device name or uuid target).

capture_list.name: List captures
capture_list.description: Returns every stored capture (or the one named by capture_id) with its result block, the interpreted window and its read-time resolved target.

capture_id.name: Capture ID
capture_id.description: Return only this capture. Omit to return every capture.

capture_start.name: Start a live capture
capture_start.description: Starts a live capture ("on now"). Stop it with capture_stop; read the result with capture_list. Only one capture can be open at a time.

label.name: Label
label.description: A short label for this capture.

target_type.name: Target type
target_type.description: What the capture teaches: a new device, an existing Review candidate, or a confirmed device.

target.name: Target
target.description: A new device's name; a candidate's name or signature id; a confirmed device's name or uuid when no device is picked.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Pick a confirmed PowerGuesser device (a shortcut for a device name or uuid target).

capture_stop.name: Stop a live capture
capture_stop.description: Stops the open live capture and returns at once with state resolving. The snapped result appears after the settle wait in capture_list and Review.

capture_id.name: Capture ID
capture_id.description: Stop this capture. Omit to stop the one open capture.

capture_cancel.name: Cancel a capture
capture_cancel.description: Cancels an open capture. Idempotent on a finished capture.

capture_id.name: Capture ID
capture_id.description: Cancel this capture. Omit to cancel the one open capture.

capture_delete.name: Delete a capture
capture_delete.description: Deletes a stored capture and returns whether its preview card was removed. Idempotent on an id that no longer exists.

capture_reassign.name: Re-assign a capture
capture_reassign.description: Moves a capture to a new target. The only action that rewrites a capture's target; a device target recomputes its read-only replay check.

target_type.name: Target type
target_type.description: What the capture teaches: a new device, an existing Review candidate, or a confirmed device.

target.name: Target
target.description: A new device's name; a candidate's name or signature id; a confirmed device's name or uuid when no device is picked.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Pick a confirmed PowerGuesser device (a shortcut for a device name or uuid target).

no_endpoint.message: Configure an LLM endpoint in the PowerGuesser options first.

no_consent.message: Confirm the PowerGuesser data-sharing notice under Settings > System > Repairs first.

capture_ambiguous_local_time.message: The start or end time is ambiguous in the Home Assistant time zone ({value}); it falls in a repeated hour. Provide a time with an explicit offset.

capture_nonexistent_local_time.message: The start or end time does not exist in the Home Assistant time zone ({value}); it falls in a skipped hour. Pick another time.

capture_already_open.message: A capture is already open ({capture_id}); stop or cancel it first.

capture_target_unknown.message: No capture target matches {target}. Visible choices: {choices}.

capture_target_ambiguous.message: The capture target {target} is ambiguous; it matches more than one target: {choices}.
